summary: The custody pilot for FS-GG/.github#4710 (C-J1) is .github/workflows/wasm-custody-pilot.yml, job custody-pilot. It runs only on workflow_dispatch; pull requests run static controls. It runs pilot_sequence from the inline caller in fable-reference-public.yml inside one sudo systemd-run delegated unit (TasksMax=4096, MemoryMax=8G, RuntimeMaxSec=1800), with a 30-minute job for runs 1 and 2 and 40 minutes for run 3, contents: read and no secrets. Each admission admits exactly one dispatch. Validation requires main, admitted_ref equal to SHA, WORKFLOW_SHA and the checked-out head, the recorded admission URL, the workflow identity, the unit name and attempt 1. The first run (admission 6346457201) is retained evidence. The second run (admission 6347853904) adds the following. A pre-unit step installs exactly deps[ubuntu24.04-x64].webkit of the pinned playwright-core 1.63.0 bundle (51 packages, no tools group) and records dpkg-query before and after, the diff, the apt sources and the exit code; it runs only on attempt 1, with a 5-minute timeout and continue-on-error, apt-get update does not gate the install, it is never fatal, and results are labelled ubuntu-24.04 + recorded packages. The unit's properties are read back via systemctl show as a managed group. A survivor case per family uses a detached holder that keeps the browser alive after the leader exits. leftover-retired requires a launch-descendant browser process (not only the holder) among the residual pids, followed by contained retirement; a holder launch failure is kept as evidence. Forced cases record observedBrowserMembers, the launched browser processes in the owner's member sample; that sample covers every member observed, so it does not show which processes were held at the deadline. Hidden evidence files are included. Per family there are normal, forced, exit and survivor cases plus the Chromium library scan; stock host validation runs per family and is non-fatal. Each case counts only when contained, removed and free of escapes. Lessons: a line edited into the inline caller must keep the block's 10-space YAML indent (now guarded together with node --check of the pilot scripts); Playwright kills its browser when the launching process exits, so survivor retirement needs a detached holder; and sudo is unavailable inside a NoNewPrivileges unit, so host packages must be installed before the unit. Installed C stays held. The third and final run (admission 6349235037) bounds the install as timeout -k 15 480 apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=5 -o Acquire::http::Timeout=30 (update bounded to 60 s), with a 10-minute step and a 40-minute job. An EXIT trap always writes the update and install exit codes, the dpkg after-state (after waiting up to 20 s for dpkg, which apt runs outside timeout's process group), the diff and a step-complete marker; TERM and INT record their own status. The pilot derives attempted and timed-out from explicit step markers (states installed, install-timed-out, install-interrupted, install-failed, install-not-reached, not-attempted; an update timeout is recorded separately) and counts served fetches (Get lines) per host. The runner's mirror+file list is recorded before and after; on GitHub runners it already ranks Azure at priority 1 and archive.ubuntu.com at priority 2, and a bare archive.ubuntu.com entry is appended only if absent (apt ranks untagged entries last). A post-step check records any remaining apt or dpkg process. If that install fails to complete, WebKit on hosted runners is a recorded residual and no fourth run follows.
title: Dispatch-only WASM custody pilot admits one run per admission; the third bounds and records the WebKit apt install
